reasoning: Both are serious, buildable plans covering all three environments. A is a single coherent pass: brief goals map one-to-one onto the three environments plus trust/reproducibility; spec features trace to those goals; architecture components cover every requirement ID; no stale or superseded text. Its RL plan is sound and realistic for the ~1h-per-env budget (3 seeds, <=60 min per run, staged predator-prey with stage 3 explicitly allowed not to converge, SB3 reference check gated before moving to the next world). B is more detailed and in places more testable (exact physics numbers, worked GAE/return examples, checked observation sizes 6/7/13/22/17, a cross-play progress rule, opponent pool), but it carries clear marks of incremental revision: the brief was never re-centred on the three environments (Goal 5 is Snake-only, Goal 4 is an architecture feature, there is no goal for continuous control or co-evolution, and success lists reward shaping/exploration concepts that are never planned), the spec summary still calls itself 'the first milestone', QR-01..QR-04 are worded only for Snake, PPO-11 sits between PPO-08 and PPO-09, the spec has many '(changed/added 2026-10-14)' tags and process notes ('chosen by Claude for review'), architecture keeps superseded AD-02/AD-10, a struck-through risk and a '— AD-10' comment on the AD-15 interface, and both idea files still list Open questions that the spec has already resolved. B's per-run budget (<=10 min, 5 seeds, parallel processes) is also tighter and riskier for hand-written PPO than the user's ~1h per env. B is 2.5x longer for roughly equal build guidance. A wins on consistency, right-sizing and ease of finding what to build next; B wins on testable precision.
